checks.def12_jet_form: IsJetStructure G J has five fields. `iso` says every jet is the germ of an OpenPartialHomeomorph at a point of its source (« jets d'isomorphismes », plan F3). `isEtaleOpen` is « ouvert » (see issue 1). `source_surjective` is 1°. `smul_mem` and `transitive` are 2°: « opère » (the action preserves J and fibres) and « transitivement sur chaque fibre ». exists_hasGroupoid_jets_eq_iff: J is the jets of some (G,X)-structure iff IsJetStructure G J. maximalAtlas_eq_of_jets_eq: J determines the maximal atlas. So {structures up to maximal atlas} ≃ {jet structures}, which is exactly 'the structure is the datum J(V)'. No connectedness, Hausdorffness or analyticity is used: a generalisation. Faithful to 1° and 2°
checks.def12_revetement: Proved only as sets: the fibres are free G-orbits (eq_one_of_jetSMul_eq, needs IsAnalyticAction) and the jets over a chart domain are {g • jet y e}, each for a unique g (mem_jets_iff_existsUnique). There is no TopologicalSpace on Jet M X, so neither « J(V) ouvert » nor « revêtement » has a topological counterpart (issue 1)
checks.mark_def13: IsCompatibleChart G e := ∀ x ∈ e.source, jet x e ∈ jets G X M. This is « tous ses jets appartiennent à J(V) » verbatim, for a chart of U = e.source onto the open e.target. isCompatibleChart_iff ties it to the maximal atlas. The J(V) used is the one proved to be a Déf. 12 jet structure, so the unproved « revêtement » remark of Déf. 12 does not affect it. « carte compatible » is terminology. Earned
checks.mark_prop3: existsUnique_structure_of_atlas_printed: charts f i covering M (`hcov`), one g_ij on each NONEMPTY U_i ∩ U_j with f_i = g_ij • f_j there; it concludes a (G,X)-structure with every f_i compatible (Déf. 13), unique up to maximal atlas among all such structures. checks.prop1_counterexample: not_prop1_of_disconnected is correct. Take V = ℝ¹ (chartedSpaceSelf, connected, T2, second countable) and U = {y<1} ∪ {y>2}. φ₁ = cxChart is compatible (translation by 10 on {y>2}) and φ₂ = id_U is compatible. issues.problem: The « J(V) est un revêtement » sentence is not proved topologically, and « ensemble ouvert » is a stand-in. IsEtaleOpen is the basic-open property of the étalé topology. No topology on Jet M X exists, so IsEtaleOpen is never proved equivalent to openness, and the checklist's '✓ carried' overstates. Missing for the mark: (1) `instance : TopologicalSpace (Jet M X) := generateFrom {S | ∃ (f : M → X) (W : Set M), IsOpen W ∧ S = (fun y => jet y f) '' W}`; (2) `isOpen_iff_isEtaleOpen : IsOpen J ↔ IsEtaleOpen J` (⇐ union of basics, ⇒ for a basic set by Germ.coe_eq + Eventually.eventually_nhds); (3) `isCoveringMap_jets [IsAnalyticAction G X] : IsCoveringMap (fun j : jets G X M => j.1.1)`, with G discrete. The trivialisation over e.source is (y, g) ↦ g • jet y e. Its sheets {jet y (g • e) | y ∈ e.source} are basic opens, pairwise disjoint by mem_jets_iff_existsUnique. Rigidity is needed here: without it the sheets can overlap and J(V) is non-Hausdorff, not a covering. Prop. 2's proof (wave 3) needs exactly this topology

fidelity_summary: The atlas definition (plan F2) and Déf. 12's jet definition are proved equivalent in both directions, with the structure determined by its jets. 1° and 2° are rendered faithfully. Only the closing « revêtement » sentence, and the topological meaning of « ouvert », are not formalized, so Déf. 12 is rightly partial. Déf. 13 is verbatim and its mark is earned. Prop. 3 is proved as printed plus a strong form, and its mark is earned. Prop. 1 is proved for connected U, with a correct counterexample in the paper's own setting for disconnected U. The Remarque is proved for the standard hemisphere chart and for every equivariant open embedding, and is rightly unmarked.
prop1_reading_or_finding: A finding, under DEC-27, and a fair literal reading. (i) « soit U un ouvert de V » is unambiguous: the period's word for a connected open set is « domaine » or « ouvert connexe ». (ii) Plan F6's connectedness is a reading of « variété » (Déf. 12's « convexe » [sic]); U is never called a variété, neither in Prop. 1 nor in Déf. 13 (« carte d'un ouvert U d'une variété »). (iii) Benzécri states connectedness when he needs it: « simplement connexe » in Prop. 2, two lines later. (iv) The one-line proof « résulte facilement du 2° de la définition 12 » is analytic continuation over U, which uses connectedness of U: an omitted hypothesis its proof uses, the DEC-27 case. (v) The counterexample lives in the paper's own category: V = ℝ¹ is connected, Hausdorff and second countable. The author MAY instead rule it an evident omission, as DEC-114 did for Déf. 2's « linéaire »: the row would then be closed with U connected and nonempty, the counterexample kept as a remark. That is a ruling, not something the code decides.

The Remarque: is « canoniquement associée » meant as 'determined by the jets GS ∘ j ∘ J(V)' (proved), or does it also require independence of the choice of j (not proved)?
